37: /-- If `b : ι → M` and `c : κ → N` are bases then so is `fun i ↦ b i.1 ⊗ₜ c i.2 : ι × κ → M ⊗ N`. -/
38: def tensorProduct (b : Basis ι S M) (c : Basis κ R N) :
39:     Basis (ι × κ) S (M ⊗[R] N) :=
40:   Finsupp.basisSingleOne.map
41:     ((TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.congr b.repr c.repr).trans <|
42:         (finsuppTensorFinsupp R S _ _ _ _).trans <|
43:           Finsupp.lcongr (Equiv.refl _) (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.rid R S S)).symm
44: 
45: @[simp]
46: theorem tensorProduct_apply (b : Basis ι S M) (c : Basis κ R N) (i : ι) (j : κ) :
47:     tensorProduct b c (i, j) = b i ⊗ₜ c j := by
48:   simp [tensorProduct]
49: 
50: theorem tensorProduct_apply' (b : Basis ι S M) (c : Basis κ R N) (i : ι × κ) :
51:     tensorProduct b c i = b i.1 ⊗ₜ c i.2 := by
52:   simp [tensorProduct]
53: 
54: @[simp]
55: theorem tensorProduct_repr_tmul_apply (b : Basis ι S M) (c : Basis κ R N) (m : M) (n : N)
56:     (i : ι) (j : κ) :
57:     (tensorProduct b c).repr (m ⊗ₜ n) (i, j) = c.repr n j • b.repr m i := by
58:   simp [tensorProduct]

62: /-- The lift of an `R`-basis of `M` to an `S`-basis of the base change `S ⊗[R] M`. -/
63: noncomputable
64: def baseChange (b : Basis ι R M) : Basis ι S (S ⊗[R] M) :=
65:   (tensorProduct (.singleton Unit S) b).reindex (Equiv.punitProd ι)

67: @[simp]
68: lemma baseChange_repr_tmul (b : Basis ι R M) (x y i) :
69:     (b.baseChange S).repr (x ⊗ₜ y) i = b.repr y i • x := by
70:   simp [baseChange, tensorProduct]
71: 
72: @[simp]
73: lemma baseChange_apply (b : Basis ι R M) (i) :
74:     b.baseChange S i = 1 ⊗ₜ b i := by
75:   simp [baseChange, tensorProduct]

140: This is a computable alternative to `LinearEquiv.ofInjective`, and a bidirectional version of
141: `LinearMap.rangeRestrict`. -/
142: def ofLeftInverse [RingHomInvPair σ₁₂ σ₂₁] [RingHomInvPair σ₂₁ σ₁₂] {g : M₂ → M}
143:     (h : Function.LeftInverse g f) : M ≃ₛₗ[σ₁₂] (LinearMap.range f) :=
144:   { LinearMap.rangeRestrict f with
145:     toFun := LinearMap.rangeRestrict f
146:     invFun := g ∘ (LinearMap.range f).subtype
147:     left_inv := h
148:     right_inv := fun x =>
149:       Subtype.ext <|
150:         let ⟨x', hx'⟩ := LinearMap.mem_range.mp x.prop
151:         show f (g x) = x by rw [← hx', h x'] }
152: 
153: @[simp]
154: theorem ofLeftInverse_apply [RingHomInvPair σ₁₂ σ₂₁] [RingHomInvPair σ₂₁ σ₁₂]
155:     (h : Function.LeftInverse g f) (x : M) : ↑(ofLeftInverse h x) = f x :=
156:   rfl
157: 
158: @[simp]
159: theorem ofLeftInverse_symm_apply [RingHomInvPair σ₁₂ σ₂₁] [RingHomInvPair σ₂₁ σ₁₂]
160:     (h : Function.LeftInverse g f) (x : LinearMap.range f) : (ofLeftInverse h).symm x = g x :=
161:   rfl
162: 
163: variable (f)

165: /-- An `Injective` linear map `f : M →ₗ[R] M₂` defines a linear equivalence
166: between `M` and `f.range`. See also `LinearMap.ofLeftInverse`. -/
167: noncomputable def ofInjective [RingHomInvPair σ₁₂ σ₂₁] [RingHomInvPair σ₂₁ σ₁₂] (h : Injective f) :
168:     M ≃ₛₗ[σ₁₂] LinearMap.range f :=
169:   ofLeftInverse <| Classical.choose_spec h.hasLeftInverse
170: 
171: @[simp]
172: theorem ofInjective_apply [RingHomInvPair σ₁₂ σ₂₁] [RingHomInvPair σ₂₁ σ₁₂] {h : Injective f}
173:     (x : M) : ↑(ofInjective f h x) = f x :=
174:   rfl
175: 
176: @[simp]
177: lemma ofInjective_symm_apply [RingHomInvPair σ₁₂ σ₂₁] [RingHomInvPair σ₂₁ σ₁₂] {h : Injective f}
178:     (x : LinearMap.range f) :
179:     f ((ofInjective f h).symm x) = x := by
180:   obtain ⟨-, ⟨y, rfl⟩⟩ := x
181:   have : ⟨f y, LinearMap.mem_range_self f y⟩ = LinearEquiv.ofInjective f h y := rfl
182:   simp [this]
183: 
184: /-- A bijective linear map is a linear equivalence. -/
185: noncomputable def ofBijective [RingHomInvPair σ₁₂ σ₂₁] [RingHomInvPair σ₂₁ σ₁₂] (hf : Bijective f) :
186:     M ≃ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂ :=
187:   (ofInjective f hf.injective).trans <| ofTop _ <|
188:     LinearMap.range_eq_top.2 hf.surjective
189: 
190: @[simp]
191: theorem ofBijective_apply [RingHomInvPair σ₁₂ σ₂₁] [RingHomInvPair σ₂₁ σ₁₂] {hf} (x : M) :
192:     ofBijective f hf x = f x :=
193:   rfl
194: 
195: @[simp]
196: theorem ofBijective_symm_apply_apply [RingHomInvPair σ₁₂ σ₂₁] [RingHomInvPair σ₂₁ σ₁₂] {h} (x : M) :
197:     (ofBijective f h).symm (f x) = x := by
198:   simp [LinearEquiv.symm_apply_eq]
199: 
200: @[simp]
201: theorem apply_ofBijective_symm_apply [RingHomInvPair σ₁₂ σ₂₁] [RingHomInvPair σ₂₁ σ₁₂] {h}
202:     (x : M₂) : f ((ofBijective f h).symm x) = x := by
203:   rw [← ofBijective_apply f (hf := h) ((ofBijective f h).symm x), apply_symm_apply]

644: ### The base-change of a linear map of `R`-modules to a linear map of `A`-modules
645: -/

648: section Semiring

650: variable {R A B M N P : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
651: variable [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] [Semiring B] [Algebra R B]
652: variable [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N] [AddCommMonoid P]

657: /-- `baseChange A f` for `f : M →ₗ[R] N` is the `A`-linear map `A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] A ⊗[R] N`.
658: 
659: This "base change" operation is also known as "extension of scalars". -/
660: def baseChange (f : M →ₗ[R] N) : A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] A ⊗[R] N :=
661:   AlgebraTensorModule.map (LinearMap.id : A →ₗ[A] A) f
662: 
663: @[simp]
664: theorem baseChange_tmul (a : A) (x : M) : f.baseChange A (a ⊗ₜ x) = a ⊗ₜ f x :=
665:   rfl
666: 
667: theorem baseChange_eq_ltensor : (f.baseChange A : A ⊗ M → A ⊗ N) = f.lTensor A :=
668:   rfl
669: 
670: @[simp]
671: theorem baseChange_add : (f + g).baseChange A = f.baseChange A + g.baseChange A := by
672:   ext
673:   simp [baseChange_eq_ltensor, -baseChange_tmul]
674: 
675: @[simp]
676: theorem baseChange_zero : baseChange A (0 : M →ₗ[R] N) = 0 := by
677:   ext
678:   simp
679: 
680: @[simp]
681: theorem baseChange_smul : (r • f).baseChange A = r • f.baseChange A := by
682:   ext
683:   simp
684: 
685: @[simp]
686: lemma baseChange_id : (.id : M →ₗ[R] M).baseChange A = .id := by
687:   ext; simp
688: 
689: lemma baseChange_comp (g : N →ₗ[R] P) :
690:     (g ∘ₗ f).baseChange A = g.baseChange A ∘ₗ f.baseChange A := by
691:   ext; simp

693: open AlgebraTensorModule in
694: lemma baseChange_baseChange {A B : Type*} [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A]
695:     [Semiring B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
696:     (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
697:     ((f.baseChange A).baseChange B) =
698:     (cancelBaseChange R A B B N).symm ∘ₗ
699:       (f.baseChange B) ∘ₗ (cancelBaseChange R A B B M) := by
700:   ext; simp
701: 
702: variable (R M) in
703: @[simp]
704: lemma baseChange_one : (1 : Module.End R M).baseChange A = 1 := baseChange_id
705: 
706: lemma baseChange_mul (f g : Module.End R M) :
707:     (f * g).baseChange A = f.baseChange A * g.baseChange A := by
708:   ext; simp

710: variable (R A M N)
711: 
712: /-- `baseChange` as a linear map.
713: 
714: When `M = N`, this is true more strongly as `Module.End.baseChangeHom`. -/
715: @[simps]
716: def baseChangeHom : (M →ₗ[R] N) →ₗ[R] A ⊗[R] M →ₗ[A] A ⊗[R] N where
717:   toFun := baseChange A
718:   map_add' := baseChange_add
719:   map_smul' := baseChange_smul
